title: How 8 years of social and individual learning interact to shape ecological competence in orangutans.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded 18 of the 22 files in the Dryad deposit (10.5061/dryad.ncjsxkt8d, CC0, 5.77 MB total) and parsed every table in pandas. Verified counts: time_to_independence.txt = 8,258 behaviour events (2,133 'Peering', 6,125 'Exploring') from 17 animals over 239 follows; data_all_w_zeroes.txt = 263 focal-follow rows from 21 animals (one row per follow, with peering and exploration counts); sampling_overlap.txt = 453 follows, 4,792.43 observation hours, 13 animals; unique_items_by_age.txt = 3,383 rows but only 869 distinct animal-by-food-item pairs over 20 animals and 308 item codes; knwn_fooditems.txt = 54,835 feeding records (50,542 flagged used) but 6 animals supply 88% of them; estimated_peering_and_independent_exploration_*.txt = 21 rows each. Also read the README (every column documented) and checked missing values, duplicates and per-animal row counts.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The study design (Suaq Balimbing field site, peering as the indicator of social learning, exploration as the indicator of individual learning), the statistical models used, and the claim of 'just under 7000 records'. I read the bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2025.08.27.672553) rather than the Science article, which is paywalled and not in PubMed Central.

a1_downloadable.note: Open CC0 deposit on Dryad; no login or application. The site puts an automated bot check in front of downloads, which I solved; files then matched the sizes listed by the Dryad application programming interface exactly.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Diet breadth is one groupby away: count distinct species_item_mod per animal in unique_items_by_age.txt. Behaviour type (Peering/Exploring) and per-follow event counts are literal columns. Cheap construction, not inference across sources.

a3_inputs_present.note: All covariates the paper uses are in the tables (age, sex, follow duration, food availability index, association size, observer, follow type). But food items are local Indonesian abbreviations (KULBT, SPG) with no Latin names or taxonomy identifiers, so no external item features can be attached.

a4_units_stated.note: README gives units for every column: duration in hours, age in years, counts as integers. The food availability index is an unitless site index, which is the only loose one.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS. The outcome of interest (diet breadth at independence) exists for 13 animals; the follow-level table has 263 rows from 21 animals, of which 5 animals supply 200 follows. The only table over 1,500 rows is the 8,258-row behaviour event log, but its independent unit is still 17 animals, 3 of which supply 66% of events.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Whole deposit is 5.77 MB of plain text; largest file 4.7 MB. Loads in under a second.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 4,792.43 hours and 453 follows match the preprint exactly. The abstract's 'just under 7000 records' reconciles as 2,133 peering plus 4,649 classified explorations = 6,782; the raw event log holds 8,258 rows, so the headline number is a filtered subset.

a8_label_provenance.note: Behaviour codes and food items are direct human field observations. WARNING: the deposited estimated_peering_and_independent_exploration_*.txt files are posterior estimates from the authors' own Bayesian model, so using them as features would be distilling that model, not learning biology; they would have to be recomputed from raw counts.

existing_models.name: Agent-based simulation of orangutan diet-repertoire development (Nature Human Behaviour 2025, 'Culture is critical in driving orangutan diet development past individual potentials', doi 10.1038/s41562-025-02350-y)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not a predictive model with a held-out split; it is a mechanistic simulation calibrated on 12+ years of Suaq orangutan behavioural data, judged by whether simulated diet breadth reaches adult-like levels.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Per the search abstract, that diets only reach adult-like breadth when multiple forms of social learning are included; I did not retrieve the full discussion.

integration.join_key: None — food plants are site-specific Indonesian abbreviations with no Latin binomial or taxonomy identifier, and animals are anonymised single letters
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: there is no standard identifier in these files that joins to any public resource.

controls.positive_control: Peering rate should fall with age and exploration should rise — a well-established pattern in this literature that any fitted model must recover.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the behaviour labels within follow and confirm the fit collapses to the per-animal base rate.
controls.external_validation: The Tuanan (Borneo) orangutan site has comparable peering/exploration data in the same group's earlier papers, but it is not in this deposit and I did not confirm it is openly downloadable.

honest_claim_h3: Among 13 to 21 wild Sumatran orangutans followed at one field site, animals that peered and explored more ended up eating more distinct food types by independence — a description of these 13 animals, not a model that would predict a new animal.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a young orangutan's watching and exploring behaviour over eight years to predict how many different foods it eats by independence.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per young orangutan: how often it watched others closely (peering), how often it poked at things on its own (exploration), plus age, sex, food availability and how many other apes were nearby. I verified there are 263 follow-level rows and only 13 to 21 animals.
plain_idea.predict: The number of distinct food types the animal eats on its own by about age 8, counted by human observers who identified the plant species and the part eaten during thousands of hours of direct field follows.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Primatologists and cultural-evolution researchers argue about how much great-ape skill comes from copying versus trial and error; a quantitative link would matter to orangutan rehabilitation and release programmes. But with 13 animals this is a statistics question, not a machine-learning one.

ml_idea: The only task with enough rows would be classifying each of 8,258 logged behaviour events as peering versus exploring from context (age, time of day, food availability, association size). That label is simply which behaviour the observer wrote down, the features are six coarse covariates, and the effective sample is 17 animals, so it is a mixed-effects regression dressed up as machine learning rather than a real modelling project.

effort.compute_note: Measured, not estimated: the whole deposit is 5.77 MB and every table parsed in pandas in under a second on this laptop. Cleaning would be the only real cost (Excel serial dates in one file versus 9/1/07 strings in another for the same follow number, 'Infant' versus 'infant', observer names with trailing spaces).
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the animals with a diet outcome: sampling_overlap.txt has 13, and unique_items_by_age.txt shows 14 of 20 animals have fewer than 50 food items recorded. That count kills it in two minutes.

verdict_reason: Fails killer A5 on sample size at the real unit of analysis. The data is exemplary in every other respect — CC0 on Dryad, 5.8 MB, every column documented, counts matching the paper, raw human observations rather than model outputs — but the thing worth predicting (diet breadth at independence) exists for 13 orangutans, the follow-level table has 263 rows from 21 animals with 5 animals supplying 76% of them, and the 869 distinct animal-by-food-item pairs span only 20 animals. The 8,258-row behaviour event log clears the row threshold but is still 17 animals with 3 contributing two-thirds of events, and its label is just which of two behaviours a human coded. Two further blocks: the deposited individual-level learning rates are posterior estimates from the authors' own Bayesian model (A8 circularity if used as features), and the food items are site-specific Indonesian abbreviations with no taxonomy identifier, so nothing joins to any external resource and no pretrained backbone fits this data type.
